title: Accenture, Dragos and SANS Institute Launch Foundation to Strengthen Cyber Defenses for Under-Resourced U.S. Utilities
snippet: Accenture, Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities. These utilities provide essential services but often lack resources for adequate protection for their operational technology (OT) environments.
fullText:
In its first phase, the initiative will provide cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training free of charge to up to 500 under-resourced utilities. Accenture, Dragos and SANS are making an initial combined commitment of approximately $10 million in funding and services. In addition, Elastic is supporting the initiative through technology that allows for software delivery at scale by providing the primary log storage and query engine within the Dragos Platform.

        

Many of the tens of thousands of small utilities across the U.S., particularly those serving rural or underserved communities, face limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology. This leaves the pumps, valves, substations and distribution networks that support essential services vulnerable to cyberattacks that can threaten public safety.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

To address this gap, Accenture, Dragos and SANS are launching the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to provide eligible utilities with OT cybersecurity technology, deployment support, hardware and training. The initiative builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which provides more than 100 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform. The foundation was announced at a roundtable discussion focused on strengthening the cybersecurity of utilities in Ohio, hosted by American Electric Power (AEP) subsidiary Ohio Power Company, Accenture and Dragos.

        

“Our work with America’s critical infrastructure operators has shown both the gravity of the cyber threats they face and a widening vulnerability gap—between large operators with the resources to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack those means,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “Together with Dragos and SANS, we will provide under-resourced utilities with the technology, expertise and training they need to better power and protect the communities they serve.”

        

“Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats,” said Robert M. Lee, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of Dragos. “The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost.”

        

Who qualifies, how to apply

Eligible participants include U.S. based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue. More than 97% of utilities fall below this threshold, representing more than 50,000 organizations that may need support. Participants can expect:

        

          

Access to the Dragos Platform and services to help organizations know what’s on their networks and how to address vulnerabilities and threats. Elasticsearch provides the underlying log storage and search capabilities that help Dragos deliver the platform at scale to participating utilities.

          

Accenture deployment services including expert configuration, integration and ongoing support.

          

SANS ICS/OT training to build and sustain in-house capabilities.

Hardware and infrastructure funding to purchase the equipment needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform.

          

Peer community access connecting participants to a network of utilities sharing operational experience.

        

        

“The best security technology in the world won’t protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on,” said James Lyne, CEO, SANS.

        

“Strong cybersecurity depends on many technologies working together. Elastic is committed to supporting Dragos in delivering its platform at scale, helping make advanced cybersecurity capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them,” said Ashutosh Kulkarni, CEO, Elastic.

        

Utilities interested in participating can learn more at https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.

        

About the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation

The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation is a nonprofit launched by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute. It raises and provides the funding, hardware, deployment services, and training that small, under-resourced utilities in the U.S. need to secure their operational technology environments. Visit https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.

title: TÜV SÜD and Accenture Accelerate Certification of Physical AI in Automated Factories and Warehouses with NVIDIA Technologies to Drive Manufacturing Productivity
snippet: TÜV SÜD, a globally recognized testing, inspection and certification organization headquartered in Germany, and Accenture are collaborating to accelerate the independent certification process for industrial automation with NVIDIA technologies.
fullText:
At NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026, the companies are presenting a joint concept of a “Physical AI Safety Suite” to help companies safely deploy physical AI equipment such as Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMR) alongside human workers faster. Using digital twins, AI agents and simulations, the Physical AI Safety Suite is designed to speed up the automation of factories and warehouses required to increase manufacturing productivity.

        

          

            

url

          

          

            

caption

            

NVIDIA GT Berlin 2026: TÜV SÜD and Accenture use NVIDIA technologies to help deploy robots and other physical AI equipment safely alongside human workers faster.

          

        

        

Established industry standards provide the basis for ensuring that automated facilities are designed and operated safely. An example is ISO 3691-4, which specifies safety requirements for driverless industrial trucks and systems, including AMRs. In many industrial countries, certification against such norms is mandatory before companies can commission automated facilities and deploy new physical AI equipment. Even in markets where certification is voluntary, following industry-specific standards issued by recognized standards bodies is considered best practice.

        

But navigating the intricate web of standards can slow down the adoption of physical AI-enabled automation solutions. At a medium-sized production plant, the iterative coordination, validation and acceptance of safety concepts can take several weeks.

        

From manual to simulation testing

Presented at NVIDIA GTC Berlin, the Physical AI Safety Suite partially digitizes the manual assessment of facilities, equipment and preparation of certification packages, using digital twins and AI-powered simulations. TÜV SÜD estimates that the digital process could bring production online up to 30% sooner. Not only does it reduce physical dependencies such as installed equipment and site visits; companies can also address safety and certification issues earlier to avoid costly reworks in operation.

caption

            

Using digital twins, AI agents and simulations, TÜV SÜD and Accenture’s Physical AI Safety Suite is designed to speed up the automation of factories and warehouses.

          

        

        

“Physical AI enables robotic systems to become increasingly adaptive while also paving the way for an independent, evidence-based digital certification process,” said Patrick Vollmer, CEO and Chairman of the Board at TÜV SÜD AG. “Through our Physical AI Safety Suite, which leverages simulation-generated evidence, we can support compliance-readiness much earlier in the engineering lifecycle without compromising the rigor safety standards require. Assessing automation concepts before the first robot is deployed reduces uncertainty in live operations and helps drive higher levels of safety, efficiency and performance across production and logistics.”

        

“Too often, companies test automation concepts against industry standards after the equipment, layouts and workflows have already been established,” said Sarat Maitin, Supply Chain and Engineering Lead for Accenture in Central and Eastern Europe. “The Physical AI Safety Suite brings these steps forward to when companies can still avoid safety incidents and costly rework. It also enables continuous monitoring of automated facilities. Both support faster deployment of physical AI-enabled automation needed to drive manufacturing productivity, particularly in Europe.”

        

Connected checks on three layers

The Physical AI Safety Suite concept assesses automation on three connected layers, with TÜV SÜD providing independent assessment and assurance, and retaining responsibility for certification:

        

Layer 1: Simulating industrial layouts – Where can companies deploy physical AI safely?

Using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, the open Cosmos world model platform and the NVIDIA Isaac Sim open robotics framework, the Physical AI Safety Suite virtually assess routes, clearances, mixed-use zones and collaboration areas before robots are deployed or layouts are reconfigured. Then it generates a structured evidence package for TÜV SÜD review, covering operating-zone requirements, hazard and risk reduction standards, robot integration norms and control-system safety standards.

        

Layer 2: Adding robotic fleets – How does Physical AI operate safely?

Using NVIDIA Omniverse, Cosmos and Isaac Sim, the Physical AI Safety Suite simulates robotic fleets and their behaviors to identify operational constraints and potential hazards, such as workers becoming trapped by AMRs, before deployment. During operation, the layer uses the NVIDIA Halos safety platform and the NVIDIA IGX Thor edge AI platform to identify potentially hazardous situations beyond an individual robot’s view. AI agents built with the NVIDIA Halos Outside-In Safety Blueprint extend a robot’s perception to reason and act autonomously with facility-mounted cameras. This allows fleet management systems to respond earlier to improve safety and operational efficiency.

        

Layer 3: Individual robots – What is Physical AI allowed to do?

Even equipment complying with all applicable product regulations must be tested under its intended site-specific conditions, such as load, speed, floor conditions and lighting. Using Isaac Sim and Cosmos, the Physical AI Safety Suite creates and tests a long tail of certification-relevant scenarios that real-world testing could never practically cover. This, for example, allows engineering teams to find the best placement for safety sensors well before a physical prototype exists.

Physical AI describes a mix of technologies, including digital twins, simulations, sensors, robots and AI models, which enables robots and machines to sense, decide, act and improve constantly under changing conditions and operate more autonomously in real environments. Accenture recently established a Center of Excellence that incubates, builds, scales and deploys physical AI solutions for warehouses and production facilities.

fullText:

caption

            

Digital-native construction consulting firm Avicado joins Accenture Construct to expand digital and systems consulting capabilities for capital projects owners.

          

        

        

Founded in 2015, Avicado helps clients improve project delivery through connected systems, stronger project controls and better use of data. The digital-native company specializes in implementing and integrating leading construction and project management software from Procore, Autodesk (Construction Cloud, BIM 360), Trimble (Trimble Unity construct/e-builder), Oracle (Primavera P6, Textura) and Kahua.

        

The firm also offers on-the-ground program delivery services to keep programs moving, with Avicado specialists serving as owner representatives, supporting site selection and feasibility, managing procurement services, and providing controls, schedule and document management.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

Avicado serves large project owners across data centers, transportation, government and public infrastructure, commercial real estate, education, healthcare, manufacturing, power and energy, and water and wastewater. Its team of more than 190 professionals will join Accenture Construct in the United States.

        

“Avicado brings exceptional talent and deep expertise in the digital platforms that underpin many capital programs,” said Adam J. Shaw, CEO of Accenture Construct. “It’s our next move to give owners the full breadth of capabilities they need—proven industry platforms, people and process, and AI—and enabling us to take greater accountability for client outcomes.”

        

“We have a community of great people who focus on continuous improvement, and that’s what drives impact on our clients’ programs,” said Avidahn Levin, founder and CEO of Avicado. “Joining Accenture Construct lets us bring our specialist experience to more clients and programs and gives our existing clients access to Accenture’s global capabilities, industry knowledge and technology. I’m excited for our team to grow their careers at Accenture Construct.”

        

Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

title: Accenture Federal Services and Google Public Sector Establish Gemini Launchpads to Power Purpose-Built Agents Across Federal Missions
snippet: Accenture Federal Services, a subsidiary of Accenture, and Google Public Sector today announced the deployment of Gemini launchpads, a new capability designed to help federal agencies move more quickly from agentic experimentation to mission execution at scale.
fullText:
This initiative, which builds on the recent announcement of Accenture’s Gemini Enterprise Business Group (part of the Accenture Google Business Group), provides federal agencies with a centralized hub of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to industrialize how they build, deploy, and scale enterprise agents. By embedding these specialized FDEs alongside agencies, the government can focus on delivering outcome-based, high-code agents built on Gemini, that integrate directly into core government systems of record and enable practitioners to execute complex workflows.

        

          

            

url

          

          

            

caption

          

        

        

By activating a Gemini launchpad, agencies can centrally manage the agent–from securely connecting Gemini to mission datasets and prioritizing agent use cases to rapid deployment and workforce training. This provides leadership with a single view to track performance, measure mission impact, and drive even more value from their investment in Gemini.

        

"The real opportunity to scale value for our clients is deploying these purpose-built agents to transform work at the heart of government operations,” said Ron Ash, CEO of Accenture Federal Services. “By embedding our Forward Deployed Engineers with agency teams, we're working side-by-side with our clients to help them define and rapidly solve their most critical challenges using agents to help deliver the advantage our clients need and the results they expect."

        

"Federal agencies stand at the threshold of the agentic era, where success is measured not merely by technology adopted, but by mission outcomes delivered," said Karen Dahut, CEO of Google Public Sector. "By pairing Gemini and secure cloud infrastructure with Accenture Federal Services’ deep federal acumen, we are enabling agencies to build purpose-driven agents designed for the way they work. This collaboration further moves governments beyond incremental modernization—equipping public servants with intelligent capabilities to navigate complex systems, accelerate critical decisions, and deliver at the speed of mission."

        

Accelerating Mission Impact with Specialized Engineers and Pre-Built Agents

To meet federal demand and accelerate this mission, Accenture Federal Services is training an initial cohort of Google Cloud- skilled FDEs. This training would be part of Accenture’s recently announced commitment to establish a 1,000-person FDE workforce Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group.

        

These FDEs will embed directly alongside agency teams and Accenture Federal’s functional subject matter experts to bridge the gap between technology and mission. By combining advanced Google Cloud technical skills with deep federal domain expertise, these integrated teams will build Gemini agents that address real agency challenges and unlock tangible mission value.

        

To jumpstart agency adoption, Accenture Federal Services and Google Public Sector are developing a core set of pre-built agents across common mission-critical functions including HR, finance, and supply chain. These agents are purpose-built to streamline daily operations directly within Gemini. By handling complex workflows and data-gathering behind the scenes, these agents free federal employees to focus on decision-making and strategic mission execution.

        

"Executing this vision requires a combination of the right technology and mission experience," said Garrett Berntsen, Chief AI Officer, Accenture Federal Services. "Google Public Sector provides the industry-leading infrastructure and frontier models, while Accenture Federal brings the deep domain expertise and engineering talent needed to solve complex mission challenges. Together, we are putting Google’s integrated tech stack to work to drive measurable outcomes for our customers."

        

How Agencies Can Get Started

Federal agencies can see these capabilities in action by engaging in collaborative, hands-on agent building workshops hosted jointly with Google Public Sector at The Forge in Washington, D.C. Recently launched within The Forge, The Prototyping Lab is a dedicated agentic prototyping space designed specifically to walk agency leaders through diverse, live agent experiences across various business and mission functions. During these interactive sessions, Accenture and Google Public Sector collaborate directly to identify the highest-impact agents for specific outcomes and outline a tactical roadmap to get started.

Accenture Federal Services is a US subsidiary of Accenture LLP that government agencies choose to drive impactful change. Our 15,000 people are committed to powering reinvention for the federal government with the same commercial technology, competitive drive and technical edge that is transforming global industry—ensuring that federal enterprises can be as modern, fast, and efficient as the country it serves. See how we reinvent at www.accenturefederal.com.
